EU-UK-Spain Agreement on Gibraltar (19 November 2019) covering taxation, customs, and post-Brexit trade continuity matters

Gibraltar network of bilateral Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) and Double Taxation Agreements administered by the HM Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Income Tax) with OECD/EU member states
Extension of the UK multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (MAAC) framework for exchange of information on request

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Limited Partnerships Act, Cap. 217 (Gibraltar), ss. 5-14 (formation, exempted partnership certificate, registered office); Limited Partnerships (Amendment) Act 2022 (mandatory UBO registration); Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Act 2018 (confidential central register of beneficial owners); Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar), ss. 30-48 (name governance); Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar) (money laundering offences, PEP definitions); Sanctions Act 2019 (Gibraltar) (financial sanctions); Financial Services Act 2019 (Gibraltar) (regulated activities); GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes (current edition) applied to licensed corporate service providers and banks; Criminal Justice Act 2015 (Gibraltar) (confiscation and enforcement)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the draft Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA) executed or initialed by the General Partner and all Limited Partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin of the partners; for Gibraltar-origin documents, certification by the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention state origin) OR Consular Legalization via the territorial competent authority in non-Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney (POA) appointing the Gibraltar registered agent, general partner representative, or formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of the instructing partner; for Gibraltar-issued apostilles, the Registrar of the Supreme Court of Gibraltar as designated Competent Authority under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copies of valid passports, national identity cards, and proof-of-address documents for every ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), general partner, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent issuing authority in the documents' country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and corporate good-standing certificate of the corporate General Partner (where the general partner is a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank or official corporate registry in the general partner's jurisdiction of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based Customer Due Diligence (CDD) and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) under the GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes: mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, limited partners, and authorized signatories against (i) the Gibraltar Sanctions List promulgated under the Sanctions Act 2019, (ii) the UN Consolidated List, (iii) the UK HM Treasury OFSI consolidated list as extended to Gibraltar, and (iv) the OFAC SDN List as banking best-practice for SWIFT-Wire and Letter-of-Credit payment rails; PEP status identified per the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar) definition; continuous transaction monitoring calibrated to the Low_Risk_Standard tier; negative-news, adverse-media, and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds corroboration required upon any PEP or sanctions-list hit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies House - Registrar of Companies name search and reservation portal (companieshouse.gi) of HM Government of Gibraltar
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory naming requirements under the Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar): a proposed ELP name must be rendered in Latin/Roman script; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Roman characters; permitted suffixes are 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'ELP', or 'Exempted Limited Partnership'; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name in Gibraltar and must not be calculated to deceive or mislead the public as to the nature of the business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or licensed registered agent must file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, citing the statutory basis for eligibility under the Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar) and distinguishing any allegedly conflicting registered name; supporting evidence such as trade-mark registrations, letters of non-objection from third parties, or prior user documentation must be annexed; if the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar for judicial review under the applicable Civil Procedure Rules; alternatively, where the refusal is premised on the name being misleading, an application can be made to the Minister responsible for Business or Enterprise for a statutory direction overriding the refusal; no statutory extension of the 90-day reservation window exists, and a lapsed reservation requires a fresh name-search and reservation application together with payment of the new statutory fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual, postal-only, or mail-forwarding address is NOT permissible to satisfy the statutory registered office requirement of an exempted limited partnership; a physical Gibraltar registered office supplied by a licensed corporate service provider is mandatory under the Limited Partnerships Act (Cap. 217). A serviced or virtual office may be commercially adopted for ancillary operational functions of the non-licensed Eurasia rail freight forwarding business, but substantive management and decision-making substance must remain demonstrable at the registered office and with the general partner.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 5-8% annual probability for a standard-risk, non-licensed ELP solely undertaking container block-train freight forwarding and expediting activities under ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488210; the probability rises to approximately 15-20% where the general partner is itself a GFSC-licensed entity; the Registrar of Companies and the GFSC retain statutory powers of entry under the Financial Services Act 2019 and may conduct unannounced verification visits of registered-office premises and service-provider files.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act 2019 (Gibraltar), ss. 4–19; Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar), ss. 7–9 (application of company provisions where not inconsistent); Income Tax Act (Gibraltar), s. 41 (tax-transparent treatment of partnerships).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Limited Partnerships, Gibraltar Companies House, HM Government of Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP/E — Application for Registration of an Exempted Limited Partnership and Statement of Particulars
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital or paid-up capital is required. Contributions are fixed by the Limited Partnership Agreement and may be cash, in kind, or deferred. No escrow account is required for an ordinary exempted limited partnership; if the ELP acts as a regulated private fund, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission rules may require segregation and safeguarding of investor money.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved by the corporate general partner's board of directors, effective upon registration: 1. The filing of the Statement of Particulars and payment of the statutory fee is approved. 2. The Gibraltar registered office at [address] is adopted. 3. [General Partner] is appointed as general partner and [Limited Partner] as initial limited partner, with capital contributions and profit shares as recited in the Partnership Agreement. 4. The Partnership Agreement is ratified in its entirety. 5. Authorized officers are directed to execute filings, open banking/EMI accounts, and provide all consents necessary to perfect the Exempted Limited Partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Name Reservation Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed ELP name for availability search against the Gibraltar companies and limited partnership register. Include the suffix 'Exempted Limited Partnership' or 'E.L.P.' and obtain written name clearance before filing the registration statement.
required_dossiers: Proposed ELP name
Name search and reservation request
Certificate of incorporation of corporate general partner, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as misleading, confusing, or too similar to an existing registered name, submit an alternative name or file a written objection with supporting rationale under the Limited Partnerships Act 2019, s. 6.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, execute, and notarize the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties and legal counsel; Gibraltar public notary or foreign notarial apostille
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Limited Partnership Agreement setting out capital contributions, profit-sharing, management powers, admission and withdrawal of partners, and dissolution events. Execute the agreement by the general partner and each limited partner. If the general partner is corporate, obtain its board resolution and powers of attorney. Notarize passports, proof of address, and source of funds documents.
required_dossiers: Original executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Consent of General Partner
Board resolution of corporate general partner
Certified passport copies of partners
Bank or professional reference detailing source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization or apostille is defective, re-execute the instrument under seal or obtain a fresh notarial certificate. If any signatory capacity is challenged, supply updated corporate authority evidence and curative board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Form LP/E with the Registrar and pay the official fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Limited Partnerships, Gibraltar Companies House
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form LP/E containing the ELP name, registered office in Gibraltar, registered agent details, general partner details, limited partner particulars, statement of capital contributions, and confirmation of compliance with the Limited Partnerships Act 2019. Pay the official state filing fee and obtain a formal receipt of submission.
required_dossiers: Form LP/E duly signed
Consent of registered-office provider
Statement of capital contributions (nil minimum requirement)
Certified copy of the Limited Partnership Agreement
Consent of General Partner to registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar raises a query, answer in writing within 14 calendar days. Submit an amended Statement of Particulars by way of supplementary filing. If registration is refused, file a fresh application or pursue an internal review with the Registrar supported by a legal opinion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain certificate of registration and confirm tax-transparent status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Limited Partnerships, Gibraltar Companies House; Gibraltar Income Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the Registrar to issue the Certificate of Registration for the Exempted Limited Partnership. Thereafter apply for a certification of tax-transparent treatment confirming that the ELP is not subject to Gibraltar tax on its income and that partners are taxed in their own jurisdictions, subject to the ELP's non-resident partner structure.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration issued by the Registrar
Tax status application form prescribed by the Gibraltar Income Tax Office
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
General partner and limited partner particulars
Legal opinion confirming pass-through eligibility, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Income Tax Office issues a domestic assessment, appeal within 30 days under the Income Tax Act (Gibraltar), s. 32, and submit a corrected tax-transparency election together with the partnership agreement and partner location evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration corporate and financial account setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Gibraltar financial institutions, electronic money institutions, and registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Onboard the ELP with a licensed bank or EMI in the name of the partnership. Present the Certificate of Registration, Limited Partnership Agreement, partner identification, and beneficial ownership confirmation. Appoint the registered office and registered agent, open payment rails including SWIFT wire and documentary letter-of-credit facilities, and establish internal accounting records for the tax-transparent structure.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of the ELP
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Bank or EMI account application and KYC/AML pack
Ultimate beneficial ownership statement
Registered agent acceptance memorandum
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or EMI raises UBO or source-of-funds concerns, provide a detailed ownership explanation, audited or notarized source-of-funds evidence, and revised bank forms. If rejection persists, select an alternative licensed bank or EMI authorized to accept ELP structures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar, Business Licensing Office and Trade Licensing Section
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or manufacturing operating licence is required for the ELP's rail-freight intermodal expedited forwarding activity. A Trade Licence may be required only if the ELP establishes a physical commercial premises in Gibraltar.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the ELP performs administrative freight-forwarding and logistics coordination only, with no Schedule 1 or Full EIA-triggering physical activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process emissions and no point-source effluent discharge. Office waste and ICT equipment must be routed through authorized waste carriers. If the ELP later operates warehousing or transhipment infrastructure, it must comply with Gibraltar waste management, water framework, and VOC/emission control standards applicable to industrial logistics sites.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not triggered for pure intermediary activities. If a physical office is occupied, the ELP must obtain fire safety certification under the Gibraltar Fire Safety Act, secure emergency lighting and means-of-escape inspection, obtain structural load clearance from Gibraltar Building Control for any racking, and prepare a workplace health and safety risk assessment under the Health and Safety at Work Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office of HM Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Income Tax), 132-140 Main Street, Gibraltar; official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi and Income Tax e-services at https://etax.gibraltar.gov.gi. Customs administration: HM Customs Gibraltar (Customs Department, HM Government of Gibraltar).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Gibraltar Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP) is formed under the Gibraltar Limited Partnerships Act 1995. The ELP must be registered with the Registrar of Companies, which issues the Registration Number. The ELP then applies to the Commissioner of Income Tax for a Certificate of Exemption under Section 37 of the Limited Partnerships Act, certifying that the partnership is an exempted limited partnership that does not carry on business within Gibraltar and cannot be assessed to Gibraltar income tax. Simultaneously, the ELP and each non-resident partner must apply through Form TRN / Entity Taxpayer Registration to obtain a Tax Reference Number (TRN) for correspondence, compliance screening, and bank account opening. A Certificate of Exemption and each partner's TRN are issued once statutory declarations, registered office details, and partner information are filed; there are no minimum capital requirements and no capital duty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. The principal statutory election is the irrevocable application for Exempted Limited Partnership status under Section 37 of the Limited Partnerships Act 1995, conditioned on the partnership not carrying on any business in Gibraltar and on the filing of an annual exemption certificate and non-resident partner return. Partners may also elect individual tax treatment under Gibraltar's Income Tax Act, and hybrid mismatch avoidance elections (including for UK-Gibraltar cross-border partnership structures) are available under the UK Hybrid and Other Mismatches (Prevention of Avoidance) Rules as extended to Gibraltar, to prevent double non-taxation or deduction/non-inclusion mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT or GST applicable. Gibraltar is outside the EU VAT area and imposes no value added tax, sales tax, or use tax. Indirect levies are limited to customs duties, excise duties, and a small consumption duty on specified imported goods (spirits, tobacco, mineral hydrocarbons) chargeable under the Customs Tariffs Act 2016 and the Customs, Excise and Taxes Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable for VAT/GST because no such tax exists. A customs registration obligation applies to any importer/exporter of goods irrespective of turnover; the economic operator must register with HM Customs Gibraltar as an importer/exporter of record and obtain a customs agent/declarant code to file SAD and NCTS transit declarations. There is no turnover threshold for customs registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate. Invoices may be issued in paper form subject to standard record-keeping requirements (retention for a minimum of 6 years). Customs clearances are processed through the Gibraltar Integrated Customs System, which supports electronic submission of Single Administrative Documents and New Computerised Transit System (NCTS) declarations for transit movements across the European Union and third countries; API-based machine-to-machine integration is accepted for licensed customs agents, but a human-validated digital stamp is not required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in Gibraltar because no VAT/GST regime exists and thus no 0% export VAT rate or VAT refund mechanism is available. The Gibraltar ELP's rail freight forwarding income is outside the scope of Gibraltar income tax under the exemption certificate, provided no business is carried on in Gibraltar; export freight services are therefore not subject to tax and require no export VAT refund claim. For customs duty purposes, goods exported from Gibraltar, including those moving under transit from a warehouse or freezone, are duty-free, and inward processing relief or temporary admission is available for goods subsequently exported.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / SAD Export) lodged electronically through the Gibraltar Integrated Customs System or under NCTS transit procedure
Bill of Lading, multimodal transport bill, or Fiata FBL evidencing international movement of the export container block train
CIM rail consignment note for the continental rail leg under COTIF/CIM rules
Inward/Outward Remittance Certificate or bank/FCA-conformant Foreign Exchange Certificate from a Gibraltar bank evidencing freight settlement and inward funds receipt
Commercial invoice, packing list, and weight certificate
Freight forwarding service contract, cargo insurance certificate, and the letter of credit instrument where payment is routed via Swift/Wire
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims for export duty relief or misrepresentations intended to preserve ELP exemption attract retrospective revocation of the Certificate of Exemption by the Commissioner of Income Tax, with the partnership re-assessed for all past Gibraltar-source profits as if exempt status had never existed, plus interest from the original due date. Penalties under the Income Tax Act include amounts up to 100 percent of the tax evaded and monetary penalties per uncorrected failure. False customs declarations attract fines of up to GBP 10,000 per declaration and forfeiture of the goods under the Customs Tariffs Act 2016. Where rail transit documents, bills of lading, or remittance certificates are fabricated or backdated, criminal liability for fraud, money laundering, or customs evasion may attach, and clawback of any tax refund, duty relief, or bank-facility benefit is ordered. The ELP's non-resident partners additionally remain exposed to their own residence-jurisdiction CFC/transparency rules; HM Revenue & Customs and HM Customs Gibraltar cooperate on joint audit scrutiny of Eurasian rail freight flows routed through the port of Gibraltar.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (acting as monetary anchor for the Gibraltar pound) and the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC), the competent authority for licensing, AML/CFT supervision, and foreign exchange activity regulation
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar maintains no separate exchange control regime. The Gibraltar pound is fully convertible into pound sterling at par, and both current account and capital account transactions are free from exchange control restrictions. Profit remittance, partnership distributions, capital repatriation, and loan repayments to non-residents may be effected without Central Bank approval, subject only to standard AML/CFT due diligence and documentary requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or conversion requirements apply. There is no mandatory timeline, minimum conversion ratio, or obligation to repatriate export proceeds into Gibraltar pound sterling. Freight-forwarding and logistics receipts may be held in any freely convertible currency in any GFSC-licensed bank or a permitted offshore counterparty, provided supporting trade documentation is retained for a minimum of six years under AML/CFT obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for operational disbursement support; Low for principal capital escrow and service of high-value letters of credit. Legal constraints: following Brexit, EEA EMI passporting rights do not extend to Gibraltar; any offshore digital EMI must be licensed or otherwise registered with the GFSC to hold funds or provide payment services in or from Gibraltar. Non-licensed EMIs may be used only as receiving sub-accounts for permitted outbound cash management if the main treasury relationship remains with a fully GFSC-licensed tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Full remote onboarding is generally permitted for non-resident Exempted Limited Partnerships under GFSC AML/CFT regulations where all partners are natural persons or regulated entities of equivalent standing. Live video identification and certified digital notarisation are accepted. Some tier-1 banks may require the general partner or nominated officer to attend one final remote interview; in-person attendance is not statutorily mandatory but may be requested by individual compliance committees for high-value capital escrow mandates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Gibraltar ELP with no local operating substance and domestic management and control held outside Gibraltar
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide registered office certificate, partnership deed, general partner resolutions showing commercial decision-making, bookkeeping and tax records evidencing economic substance where applicable, and a detailed annual activity projection for the transcontinental rail freight forwarding business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border rail freight revenue flows touching multiple high-risk jurisdictions or sanctioned corridors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a transport-chain compliance pack including export/import licences, movement reference numbers, cargo manifests, CMR/e-CMR waybills, rail consignment notes, mandatory sanctions screening results covering all counterparties, and an internal policy excluding sanctioned goods, arms, dual-use items, and entity-level exposure to prohibited regimes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through partnership structure with non-resident limited partners and multi-layer ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver full KYC/KYB files for the exempted limited partnership, all partners (including ultimate beneficial owners), source of wealth statements, certified copies of passports and addresses, audited financial statements or a CPA comfort letter, and the partnership deed explicitly prohibiting bearer interests and anonymous participation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the general partner's or limited partner's own bank account to the ELP's GFSC-licensed operational account. The wire message must contain the partnership's legal name and account IBAN, the partner's creditor reference, and a clearly stated purpose code such as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN' in the payment narrative, matching the capital call letter. Supporting verification must include a signed capital contribution letter, the underlying partnership agreement clause authorising the injection, source of funds evidence (such as bank statements or audited statements of wealth), and a partnership capital account reconciliation. Third-party fund remittance is prohibited; each injection must be traceable from the same beneficial owner or regulated intermediary named in the KYC file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for rail freight and intermodal transport settlements should be made through SWIFT MT103 for direct payments to rail operators, container terminal operators, inland hauliers, and customs agents, and through MT700 commercial letters of credit for high-value intermodal service contracts or when the supplier requires a documentary payment guarantee. Each payment must be matched to an underlying transport order supported by a rail waybill, CMR/e-CMR, supplier invoice, and customs declaration. Separate clearing rails are acceptable for local small-value incidental expenses, provided they are linked to the main GFSC-licensed account and included in the same periodic audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable currency forwards in EUR/USD/CHF against GIP/GBP with a term of up to 12 months, available only against documented freight, operating, and capital expenditure exposures

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in emerging-market and restricted currencies (e.g., CNH, KZT, PLN, and similar corridor currencies) subject to underlying trade documentation and GFSC-licensed counterparty execution
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-term infrastructure or rolling-stock financing where the ELP has matching multi-currency debt
Plain-vanilla call and put options on the major freight settlement currencies, where the sole purpose is hedging an identifiable trade exposure and no speculative uncovered positions are created

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of the ELP's registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GBP 10 per day (maximum GBP 1,000); persistent non-filing triggers administrative strike-off after 90 days’ notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Companies House – BOSS (Beneficial Ownership Secure Search) system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the filing date of the Annual Return (or within 42 days of the anniversary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalty up to GBP 500 for non-compliance; false declarations may attract fines up to GBP 5,000 and/or imprisonment under the Gibraltar Companies Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ELP must undergo a mandatory statutory audit if annual turnover exceeds GBP 2,000,000 AND balance-sheet gross assets exceed GBP 1,000,000, OR if the average number of employees exceeds 50; otherwise partners may file unaudited accounts with an exemption statement
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as promulgated by the IASB and applied under the Gibraltar Companies Act (Cap. 56); alternatively FRS 102 (UK GAAP) may be used by qualifying unlisted entities unless the ELP opts for full IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each calendar year, the ELP must submit an annual beneficial ownership confirmation through the Gibraltar BOSS system, declaring all partners and beneficial owners; any interim ownership change must be reported within 30 days. The confirmation must be signed by a general partner or the registered agent.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% (standard Gibraltar corporation tax rate for taxable companies)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% for a qualifying Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP). The ELP is tax-transparent and exempt from Gibraltar corporation tax on profits derived from sources outside Gibraltar where all partners are non-resident. No capital gains tax, no VAT, and no Gibraltar withholding tax on distributions apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form ELP-1 (Gibraltar Annual Exempt Limited Partnership Return) filed electronically through the Income Tax Office eServices portal (tax.gi)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months of the end of the chargeable period; for a 31 December year-end, the return is due no later than 31 December of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the ELP, Gibraltar registered partnership number, and Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (GTRN).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the ELP entity details. The general partner must be identified as the return signatory; no personal registration of non-resident partners is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the chargeable period in yyyy-mm-dd format.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same accounting period adopted by the principal non-resident partners to ease reconciliation; only one period per each ELP is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Exemption Claim and Income Source
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that all profits were derived from sources outside Gibraltar and that no Gibraltar-source income nor Gibraltar permanent establishment arose. The principal business activity must be described as transcontinental container block train expedited freight forwarding and intermodal logistics support (ISIC 5229).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If any Gibraltar-source income exists, report the amount and nature in a supplementary schedule; otherwise claim full exemption. Non-resident partners' shares of foreign income are shown as outside Gibraltar chargeability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and distribution allocations to general and limited partners for the period, including aggregate amounts paid or credited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide aggregate allocation figures only. Do not disclose individual non-resident partners to the portal; allocations to non-resident partners are stated as nil taxable in Gibraltar.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Automatic late filing penalty of GIP 250, plus GIP 50 per day of continued default up to a maximum of GIP 5,000 per return. Incorrect returns attract a GIP 100 fixed penalty plus a tax-geared penalty of up to 100% of the understated tax. The Commissioner may also raise anti-avoidance assessments and initiate strike-off procedures for persistent non-filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% – Gibraltar does not impose dividend or profit distribution withholding tax on amounts paid by a company or an Exempted Limited Partnership to its partners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since distributions from an ELP attract no Gibraltar withholding tax, no DTA relief application is necessary for outbound distributions. For inbound treaty benefits in source countries (e.g., the UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation Arrangement), the partner must obtain a Gibraltar Tax Residence Certificate from the Income Tax Office, file the relevant source-country treaty claim form, and provide a declaration of beneficial ownership. The TRC is issued only after confirming the ELP has met annual filing, substance, and AML obligations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rate for interest and royalties paid by an exempt ELP to non-residents is 0% provided such payments are at arm's length and the ELP remains non-resident-owned and without Gibraltar-source business profits. Under the UK-Gibraltar DTA, qualifying interest and royalty payments may be exempt from source-State income tax. Payments related to the freight forwarding operation (e.g., locomotive leasing, transhipment facility royalties, and cargo financing letters of credit) must be supported by documentation to substantiate the arm's-length nature.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: GIP 1,000,000 – aggregate cross-border controlled transactions threshold requiring preparation of a Local File and Master File. A Country-by-Country Report is separately required where ultimate group revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Gibraltar Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) 2019 apply to entities deriving gross income from relevant activities including distribution and service centre business. A rail freight and intermodal expediting ELP (ISIC 5229) will likely be classed as a distribution and service centre where it earns fees from logistics coordination, contract procurement, cargo documentation, and shipment scheduling. The ELP must therefore exercise management and control in Gibraltar, maintain proportionate staff and premises, and perform core income-generating activities in Gibraltar such as negotiating freight rates, issuing transport documents, managing intermodal connections, and administering collection/payment flows. A pure pass-through ELP with no physical substance in Gibraltar will fail the ESR unless it can demonstrate that all gross income arises outside the scope of relevant activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Misuse of ELP Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming full exemption from Gibraltar income tax while carrying on freight forwarding or intermodal logistics operations managed from within Gibraltar, or allowing the ELP to be used as a named carrier in contracts made and performed in Gibraltar while all profits are attributed to offshore partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner will re-assess the under-declared profits at the 12.5% corporate rate, add interest from the due date, and impose a penalty of up to 100% of the undeclared tax. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion may lead to an unlimited fine and imprisonment for up to 7 years on indictment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the ELP veil where the general partner and its directors signed false exemption declarations. Directors are jointly and severally liable for restitution of tax, subject to confiscation orders, travel bans, and disqualification from holding directorships in Gibraltar for up to 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transferring profits from pan-Eurasia rail freight operations to the Gibraltar ELP through unmapped intercompany mark-ups on container block-train haulage, terminal handling, and expedited forwarding services without contemporaneous Local/Master File documentation or a valid benchmark consistent with the arm's-length principle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: An adjustment to taxable profits plus interest and a tax-geared penalty of up to 100% of the corrective assessment. Failure to produce mandatory transfer pricing documentation also attracts a fixed penalty of GIP 10,000 per controlled transaction, with automatic escalation to daily penalties for continued obstruction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who directed or approved unwarranted transfer pricing adjustments can be sued for the resulting tax penalties and are personally exposed to civil fraud claims. In cross-border cases, the UK-Gibraltar exchange-of-information provisions may lead to joint liability proceedings between the associated enterprises and their directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a pure paper ELP with no physical presence in Gibraltar: no employees, no board meetings in Gibraltar, no control over transport contracts, no invoicing or cargo documentation performed in Gibraltar, and no bank account in the territory, while generating freight forwarding and intermodal service income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-compliance with the Economic Substance Regulations triggers a fine of up to GIP 100,000 per relevant activity per financial year and daily default penalties. Persistent breaches lead to strike-off from the Gibraltar Register of Companies and denial of the ELP's exempt tax status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and responsible officers face personal fines of up to GIP 500,000, disqualification orders, and travel bans issued by the Supreme Court. Where unpaid tax follows loss of exemption, shareholders and directors may be held liable for the corporate tax debt under the veil-piercing provisions of the Gibraltar Companies Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify the ultimate beneficial owners of the ELP, failure to file the beneficial ownership register with the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit, processing freight payments through SWIFT wire or letters of credit without adequate KYC safeguards, or omitting suspicious transaction reports in connection with sanctioned Eurasian rail corridors or mis-invoiced logistics cargo.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to GIP 200,000 and imprisonment up to 10 years for money laundering; failure to submit a suspicious activity report attracts separate criminal liability. Civil penalties of up to GIP 250,000 and confiscation of freight-related gains may be imposed under the Proceeds of Crime Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and the ELP's general partner cannot hide behind the corporate form. Individuals involved in facilitating mis-invoicing or transporting sanctioned cargo are personally liable for civil restitution, subject to worldwide freezing orders and travel bans, and may be sentenced to up to 14 years' imprisonment for serious money laundering offences.
